maria (Support): FYI customer hit TLS failures on their Private endpoint right after our cert rotation — started ~03:45 UTC. curl shows 'SSL: certificate verify failed'. They see 502/503 from API layer. :warning:
kevin (SRE): Do we have the customer domain + any recent rotation logs?
kevin (SRE): Also, can they repro with openssl s_client so we can see the chain?
maria (Support): Domain is api.acme-corp.internal (customer private host). I asked for an openssl dump, they sent this snippet: ```openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.acme-corp.internal:443  -servername api.acme-corp.internal``` ```CONNECTED(00000003) depth=0 C = US, O = Acme, CN = api.acme-corp.internal verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate --- Certificate chain 0 s:/CN=api.acme-corp.internal i:/CN=acme-intermediate --- 1 s:/CN=acme-intermediate i:/CN=ISRG Root X1 --- END CERTIFICATE```
kevin (SRE): Hmm that output suggests the server is sending leaf + intermediate but maybe the order is leaf then intermediate then root (which is okay) — unless intermediate is missing or the intermediate itself is signed by a different root we expect. Could also be that the endpoint is *not* sending the fullchain (client's verification needs the intermediate).
robin (Infra): @kevin tagging in to check our rotation job. Do we have any recent rotator failures for Private? eng-oncall-bot: Rotation job deploy-rotator-v2 executed at 2026-03-24T03:41:12Z, status: success, artifacts: cert-package-20260324-0341.tar.gz
kevin (SRE): Maria, one more ask: can you run `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.acme-corp.internal:443 -servername api.acme-corp.internal -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt` on a host that fails and paste full verify output? Also check `curl -v https://api.acme-corp.internal/health`
maria (Support): Customer ran curl -v: ```* Connected to api.acme-corp.internal (10.20.30.40) port 443 (#0) * ALPN, offering http/1.1 * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1) * TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1) * SSL: certificate verify failed```
maria (Support): They also attached their LB config; looks like their load balancer expects a fullchain.pem and key. They said they uploaded what we provided.
kevin (SRE): Two possible culprits: 1) our rotation package omitted the intermediate or put chain in wrong ordering; 2) the customer's LB stripped intermediates (some LBs only accept leaf+intermediate but expect specific order). Another possibility: OCSP/CRL egress blocked so client can't verify revocation status, but usually that yields different errors.
robin (Infra): I'm pulling the artifact now. Quick check of cert-package-20260324-0341 shows certs/leaf.pem and certs/intermediate.pem but the fullchain created by our packaging script concatenates files in lexicographic order — I see intermediate.pem then leaf.pem, which results in intermediate before leaf in the bundle. That can cause some chain-validation edge cases for some clients that expect leaf first. That's a bug in rotator script.
kevin (SRE): Good catch. That would explain 'unable to get local issuer certificate' on certain clients. Some TLS stacks require leaf first.
maria (Support): Customer is behind a hardware LB (vendor: F5) that expects leaf then intermediate. They said they uploaded our fullchain.pem directly from the portal.
kevin (SRE): Short-term workaround: ask customer to upload concatenated bundle with leaf first. Command to produce that on our side: ```cat certs/leaf.pem certs/intermediate.pem > corrected_fullchain.pem``` Then upload corrected_fullchain.pem into LB.
robin (Infra): I'll open an internal bug. Root cause: rotation packaging script lists certs by filename and concatenates in that order; when intermediate filename sorts before leaf it's wrong. Fix: ensure leaf is first or explicit ordering when building fullchain. I'll push a patch to rotator and redeploy.
kevin (SRE): Also check whether their LB is blocking OCSP traffic — ask them to allow egress to ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org and CRL endpoints; but first prioritized fix is bundle ordering.
maria (Support): I passed the workaround and they tested: after uploading corrected_fullchain.pem they report TLS handshake succeeds and API calls are passing again. :tada:
robin (Infra): Patch PR created: rotator#482 — adds deterministic ordering and unit test for bundle generation. I will also add a post-rotation verification step that does an openssl s_client check against exported bundle.
kevin (SRE): Can we add a quick monitor to catch this class of issue earlier? Maybe a synthetic probe from private edge that validates cert chain ordering for customers after rotation.
robin (Infra): Good idea. I'll add a healthcheck job to rotation pipeline to run `openssl s_client -showcerts` and validate chain order/verify on a sandbox endpoint.
maria (Support): Customer is happy, they want confirmation when we roll out the fix globally. I'll keep the ticket open until patch is deployed and validated.
kevin (SRE): Thanks everyone. I'll update INC-2026-411 and mark as high priority until rotator patch is live.
eng-oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-411 created and assigned to infra/rotator oncall.
maria (Support): Closing loop with customer now, leaving follow-up note that we changed packaging and added verifications. If customer still sees intermittent TLS errors we will reopen.
robin (Infra): Will post deploy ETA once rotator patch merges. Estimated next deploy window: 2026-03-24T06:00Z.
maria (Support): Thanks :white_check_mark:
